newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end higher on fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end higher on fresh demand.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closes 35 rupees higher at 4,830 rupees per 10 grammes on fresh seasonal buying while the supply is at a low ebb.
** Gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) closes 400 rupees up at 56,500 rupees per piece. It was down by 200 rupees per piece on Monday after gaining 400 rupees last week.
** Silver (.999) finishes 20 rupees higher at 6,980 rupees per kg as fresh industrial buying helps prices to bounce back. Silver was down by 40 rupees per kg on Monday.

Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees higher at 4,830 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,795 rupees as fresh seasonal buying helped prices to bounce back while arrivals remained low, dealer said.

Reports that custom officials had seized smuggled gold worth 10 million rupees at Bombay's international airport also helped the uptrend in the open market where traders feared a shortage of supplies. Gold was down 15 rupees per 10 grammes on Monday.

Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes each) settled 400 rupees higher at 56,500 rupees against the previous close of 56,100 rupees. They were down 200 rupees per piece on Monday but were up by 400 rupees last week.

Silver (.999) closed 20 rupees higher at 6,980 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,960 rupees on renewed industrial buying reduced arrivals of imported silver kept offerings low. Silver was down 40 rupees per kg on Monday.
The Bombay Bullion market will remain closed on Wednesday for a Hindu festival. The market will reopen for trading on Thursday.
